$meta.purpose: Research artifact for editorial review only. NOT an import file. Do NOT pass to seedCareerWorld.
$meta.canonical_invariant: 780 total careers; 15 fixed worlds; one world per production career; variable per-world allocation. No canonical IDs are minted here - UUIDs are generated at import time.

evidence_ladder.label: national_classification
evidence_ladder.meaning: National / authoritative occupation classification (e.g. ONS SOC 2020, BLS OOH, O*NET, ESCO)

evidence_ladder.label: industry_framework
evidence_ladder.meaning: Industry / professional framework (e.g. SFIA, NICE/NIST SP 800-181, IEEE/ACM curricula, PMI, TOGAF, DAMA)

evidence_ladder.label: market_evidence
evidence_ladder.meaning: Market evidence (job-postings analyses, labour-market reports, certification bodies)

evidence_ladder.label: documented_position
evidence_ladder.meaning: Documented primary positions at named employers / real practitioner base

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Canonical identity; web/frontend/backend/full-stack/mobile vocabulary resolved as aliases (see merge candidates).
candidates.resolution: Anchor career; no dedupe required.
candidates.rationale: Anchor career of the World. Builds, maintains and ships software systems; the broadest and most empirically dense technology occupation. All frontend/backend/full-stack/web titles are terminology variants of this single canonical identity, not separate careers.
candidates.basis: Multi-country national classifications treat software developer as a core established occupation.
editorial_flags: seed improvement recommended in report G: sharpen canonical description; web-developer alias needs explicit SEO handling

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Genuinely distinct specialisation of software development.
candidates.resolution: Keep as distinct career.
candidates.rationale: Distinct body of knowledge (game engines, rendering, physics, real-time systems, tooling) with its own industry and progression. Genuinely separate occupation function, while still a software-engineering specialisation.
candidates.basis: Recognised specialisation across game studios and academic programmes.

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Overlaps systems-software-engineer at low-level boundary; firmware sub-roles are aliases.
candidates.resolution: Keep distinct; firmware/embedded-application vocabulary resolved as aliases.
candidates.rationale: Software for microcontrollers, RTOS, and hardware-adjacent systems. 2026 hiring data supports distinct sub-roles (embedded systems vs firmware vs embedded-application). Firmware is an alias specialization of this canonical identity, not a separate career.
candidates.basis: Consistent distinct-demand profile across hiring platforms; clearly separated from generic software development.

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Overlaps embedded-systems-engineer at the boundary (OS/toolchain vs device software).
candidates.resolution: Keep distinct at discipline level.
candidates.rationale: Low-level software: OS kernels, runtimes, compilers, toolchains, system libraries. Distinct working domain from application development and from embedded (device) work, though both are low-level.
candidates.basis: Stable systems-programming discipline with its own community and hiring pool.

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Distinct specialist discipline (rendering pipelines, GPU programming); overlaps game-developer at engine boundary.
candidates.resolution: Keep distinct; relations to game-developer and xr-developer.
candidates.rationale: Real-time and offline graphics: rendering, GPU compute, pipelines used in games, film/VFX, CAD and browsers. A distinct body of knowledge with its own industry demand beyond game development alone.
provenance: industry positions (film/VFX, chip vendors, software vendors)
candidates.basis: Established graphics discipline with dedicated industry and conference ecosystem.

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Boundary consideration: communication-heavy roles could claim World 09; primary function is engineering tooling.
candidates.resolution: Keep in World 01 pending editorial ratification.
candidates.rationale: Technical staff who build SDKs/docs/tooling and bridge a platform to its developer community. A real, recurring technical function with its own skill mix (engineering + communication).
provenance: documented positions at major platform companies
candidates.basis: Named DevRel roles staffed continuously across developer-platform employers for a decade.
editorial_flags: boundary: developer advocate could be argued into World 09
candidates.cross_world: Possible World 09 (Media & Communication) boundary; editorial to ratify.

candidates.resolution: Merge into software-developer as alias covering frontend/backend/full-stack/web specialist terminology.
candidates.rationale: Distinct SOC unit in some taxonomies (e.g. ONS web design/development) but functionally a stack focus within software development. Failing to alias creates duplicated SEO surfaces.
candidates.basis: Some classifications split web roles; editorial recommends a single canonical identity.
editorial_flags: SEO alias mapping must be authored in profile docs (doc 03 + 06)

candidates.resolution: Merge into software-developer as platform specialisation (iOS/Android/cross-platform).
candidates.rationale: Strong recruiting terminology but the same occupation function as software development with platform framing. Recommend alias rather than separate career to protect canonical identity.
candidates.basis: Consistent recruiter vocabulary; not evidence of a distinct occupation.
editorial_flags: alternative position: keep as specialist career - editorial to ratify

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Complementary to machine-learning-engineer (ships products on foundation models vs trains/operates custom models) and data-scientist.
candidates.resolution: Keep distinct with explicit relations.
candidates.rationale: Largest AI hiring category (43,480 US postings in a 2026 hiring analysis). Builds AI products on foundation models: retrieval-augmented generation, agents, evaluation, guardrails, deployment. The historical prompt-crafting title of 2023 has folded into this identity.
candidates.basis: Distinct, dominant and recurring hiring category; foundational-model product engineering is now standard practice.
editorial_flags: seed improvement recommended in report G: upgrade seed from emerging to current and sharpen scope vs MLE

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Complementary pair with ai-engineer; not a duplicate.
candidates.resolution: Keep distinct (trained-model development/ops vs foundational-model product integration).
candidates.rationale: Training, serving and operating custom/purpose-built models (PyTorch, feature engineering, pipelines, MLOps practices). 2026 taxonomy splits AI Engineer from ML Engineer - genuinely distinct functions with distinct postings.
provenance: 2026 AI vs ML role-segmentation market research
candidates.basis: Recurring distinct hiring category across employers and job boards.
editorial_flags: seed model progression references ml-platform-engineer - align terminology with this canonical identity

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Overlaps ai-engineer and machine-learning-engineer at evaluation/experimentation boundaries.
candidates.resolution: Keep distinct; statistics/experimentation identity.
candidates.rationale: Statistics, experimentation, and model-driven insight. Distinct from ML engineering (productionisation) and data engineering (pipelines). Retained as seed canonical career.
candidates.basis: Widely classified and tracked occupation.

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Overlaps C1 robotics at perception boundary.

candidates.basis: Stable specialist discipline in robotics, security, medical imaging, industrial inspection.

candidates.basis: Sharp relative decline in standalone NLP-titled postings under foundation-model tooling.

candidates.duplicate_or_overlap: Distinct from engineering identities (research output vs shipped product).

Axipro analysis of 3,519 governance-hire postings across 8 EU countries
Forrester projection (60% of large enterprises to appoint Head of AI Governance by end-2026)
